newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices seen easing in 1997-Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices seen easing in 1997-Negara.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber prices are projected to ease further in 1997 due to subdued external demand with stocks still high, Bank Negara said on Friday.
The central bank did not give any forecast figure in its annual report for 1996.
Malaysia's benchmark, International Ones Ribbed Smoked Sheet spot month is currently quoted at 298.50 cents a kg.
Bank Negara said in its 1996 annual report that output of natural rubber registered a second successive year of decline in 1996, falling 0.5 percent to 1.1 million tonnes.

"This was mainly due to declining hectarage in Peninsular Malaysia (which accounted for 80.9 pct of the total area under rubber) by 0.7 pct, labour constraints, less attractive rubber prices as well as adverse weather conditions," the Bank said.
"With lower production of rubber, Malaysia had to increase rubber imports to meet the higher requirements from domestic rubber-based industries."
Malaysia, the third largest producer of natural rubber, accounted for 17.8 percent of the world's output, behind Thailand and Indonesia.
Total cultivated area under rubber fell by 0.3 percent to 1.7 million hectares in 1996.

Bank Negara did not give a figure for stocks at end-1996. But the Malaysian Rubber Research and Development Board estimated stocks at 195,211 tonnes in the first half of 1996, up 8.1 percent from the end of July 1995.
